metadata.case_name: TA XUONG v. THE INCORPORATED OWNERS OF SUN HING BUILDING

plaintiff.occupation_before: plumbing and electrical worker (employed by Shun Cheong Electrical Co.)

source: This Plaintiff falls within the Frankel Grade A, B, C of quadriplegia
injuries.icd_description: Complete lesion of cervical spinal cord

manifestations.description: The quadriplegic state involves paralysis of all four limbs.
he has no upper body mobility whatever, with the exception of his head.
he has persistent head and shoulder pain and spasms
depression is acute and likely to be long lasting
the physical relationship in a marriage has gone for all time
he is entirely dependent upon others, within or without the family, for every action essential to survival.
no prospect of a worthwhile substitute career
There is no sense of privacy

treatments_received: physiotherapy (initial thrice weekly sessions for 12 weeks and once weekly for following 12 weeks)
occupational therapy (initial weekly sessions for 6 months)
in-patient psychiatric treatment (3-week period per year)
treatments_future: annual in-patient psychiatric treatment (one 3-week period per year)
two carers to cover 24 hour period (day China Trained Nurse and night Chinese Care Assistant)

losses.description: Paralysis of all four limbs (quadriplegia) resulting in severe impairment of bodily function.
Paralysis of all four limbs resulting in inability to move and requiring full assistance.
entire dependence upon others for every action essential to survival.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: the physical relationship in a marriage has gone for all time

losses.category: Loss of ability to participate in parenthood or grandparenthood
losses.description: the ability to share in the bringing up of children has gone
Burden borne by the family and substantial disruption to family life and roles.
No prospect of a worthwhile substitute career; inability to continue previous trade as electrician/plumber.
There is no sense of privacy and significant restriction of social activities.
depression is acute and likely to be long lasting
